title: Parallel Inclusive Scan
alt: A four-element Hillis–Steele inclusive prefix scan: aligned input elements, offset-one sums, and offset-two sums with distinct copy dependencies.
strengths: Exactly four aligned element positions and two dependency stages.
Addition operators differ visually from copied values.
All specified data dependencies and final prefix expressions are readable.
limitations: Dependency illustration only; no hardware cycle or throughput claim.
Two offset-two diagonal links cross vertical pass-through lines, with no junction marks.

provenance.workflow: silicon_prepare → host semantic spec → silicon_compile → built-in image_gen

description: A mathematical dataflow figure explaining a four-element inclusive prefix scan, using two parallel Hillis-Steele stages. Input vector a=[a0,a1,a2,a3]. Offset 1 simultaneously computes b0=a0, b1=a0+a1, b2=a1+a2, b3=a2+a3. Offset 2 simultaneously computes y0=b0, y1=b1, y2=b0+b2, y3=b1+b3. Output y=[a0,a0+a1,a0+a1+a2,a0+a1+a2+a3]. Show four aligned element columns and the two offset stages, keeping copy dependencies visible and separate from addition. Dependency stages, not cycle timing; use only these exact four elements. Keep input and output row labels, restrained compact typography, and meaningful operation symbols. No hardware memory or execution units.

settings.notes: Refined academic diagram, white canvas, near-black thin lines, cool teal operand rows and restrained amber addition nodes. Four equal columns with plenty of horizontal whitespace. Top-to-bottom depth: input at top, offset 1 in middle, offset 2/output at bottom. Draw copied values as small points or plain labels and actual additions as circles with +; diagonals are appropriate because this is a scan dependency network, no elbow zigzags. Offset annotations sit unobtrusively on left. A single thin amber highlight can distinguish the offset-2 span. Avoid giant cards, dashboard headers, decorative labels, shaded panels, 3D effects. Mathematical array values must read clearly.
